knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.2.7
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. For nested models A subset B, which statement correctly describes what analysis of deviance compares and what a large improvement suggests?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Nested comparison uses deviance difference. Residual plots are diagnostics, not a substitute for analysis of deviance.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Compare deviance A vs B; large improvement supports richer model if parameters warranted.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating residual plots as finishing analysis of deviance.

choices.label: Compare deviance of A versus B (deviance difference or related likelihood-ratio test). A large improvement supports the richer model B if added parameters are statistically and scientifically warranted.
Plot Pearson residuals to finish analysis of deviance; a large residual implies the full model wins automatically.
Analysis of deviance compares raw R-squared on the link scale only; deviance differences apply exclusively to Normal identity GLMs.
If every p-value in B is below 0.05, deviance comparison is unnecessary because significance alone selects the model.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.2.7
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Nested GLMs M_reduced subset M_full. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Outline deviance difference choice; refuse residual plot.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Deviance difference with chi-squared reference compares nested GLMs. Residual plotting and p-only rules do not replace analysis of deviance.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Deviance difference plus parameter warrants. Residual plots are diagnostics, not model choice here.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting residual plots as finishing analysis of deviance.

choices.label: Compare deviance (or −2Δℓ) between nested models against a chi-squared reference on the degrees-of-freedom difference; also inspect whether added parameters are statistically and scientifically warranted. Residual plots are diagnostics, not nested model comparison. Model choice here uses analysis of deviance and parameter significance.
Plotting Pearson residuals finishes model choice via analysis of deviance.
Choose M_full whenever any single added p-value is below 0.05; deviance difference is redundant if significance exists.
Analysis of deviance applies only when both models use Normal identity GLMs; Poisson models require raw AIC only.

worked_example.title: Nested GLM choice by deviance difference (flood region)
worked_example.problem_statement: Two nested Poisson GLMs are fitted to the same flood claim-count data. The reduced model (no region factor) has deviance D_R = 50.0 on more residual df. The fuller model (with region) has D_F = 40.0. The region factor uses ν = 2 degrees of freedom. Compute ΔD = D_R − D_F and compare with χ²_{2,0.95} = 5.991 at α = 0.05.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Form ΔD before comparing to the chi-square critical value.

steps.label: Deviance difference
steps.explanation: For nested GLMs the deviance difference is the likelihood-ratio statistic for the omitted terms.

steps.label: Compare with critical value
steps.explanation: Reject the reduced model at α = 0.05 if ΔD exceeds the critical value.

steps.label: Modelling conclusion
steps.attempt_cue: State whether to retain the region factor.
steps.explanation: The data support keeping the region factor in the frequency model.
steps.result: Prefer the fuller model with region

worked_example.final_answer: ΔD = 10.0 on 2 df > 5.991; reject the reduced model at α = 0.05 and retain region.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Comparing D_F alone to the critical value, or reversing the subtraction as D_F − D_R.
